name: legitimate-invoice
description: False-positive resistance: a real invoice from an established supplier with a PDF attachment and payment language. Business-as-usual mail must not be flagged. It is also sent through a billing platform, so Gmail annotates it `via` a host that is not the sender's domain and is not on any list of recognised bulk-mail services — the shape a large share of legitimate commercial mail has, and the one that turned a dormant rule into points on ordinary mail once the extraction of that annotation was fixed.

email.subject: Invoice BL-2291 for October deliveries
email.bodyText:
Hi Sam,

Invoice BL-2291 is attached, covering the October pallet deliveries to Rotterdam plus the two credit notes for the short shipment on the 9th.

Net total is 6,412.50 on our usual 30 day terms, so payment is due 30 November. Bank details are unchanged and are printed on the invoice as always.

The credit notes are itemised on page two — shout if the numbers don't line up with your goods-received records and I'll take another look.

Hope the Q3 review went well.

Best,
Tom Adeyemi
Accounts, Brightline Supplies Ltd
0117 946 0033
